# CodeSurf for agents

CodeSurf turns your investigation into a guided code tour using an official, consistent viewer. You create tour JSON locally from the repository. Download the versioned packager and use it to produce a standalone HTML file. The packager embeds the viewer and source excerpts. Repository code stays on the user's computer.

When the user asks to "surf code" or "run CodeSurf", follow this workflow. Build and open a tour, rather than merely explaining how to create one.

## Start here

1. Read https://codesurf.io/tour-format.txt and the JSON schema at https://codesurf.io/releases/1.0.0/tour.schema.json.
2. Inspect the working example at https://codesurf.io/releases/1.0.0/example.json and the rendered demo at https://codesurf.io/releases/1.0.0/demo.html.
3. Download https://codesurf.io/releases/1.0.0/codesurf.mjs to a local working directory. This single file includes the validator and the official viewer. It requires Node.js 20.19 or newer, with no npm install or server.
4. Investigate the user's question and write tour.json using the format below.
5. Validate and render locally:
   node codesurf.mjs tour.json --validate
   node codesurf.mjs tour.json --out tour.html
6. Open tour.html in a browser, verify the tour, and give the user a clickable file link.

Use a normal file download, for example:
   curl -fsS https://codesurf.io/releases/1.0.0/codesurf.mjs -o codesurf.mjs

To try the complete tool before investigating:
   node codesurf.mjs --example > demo.json
   node codesurf.mjs demo.json --out demo.html

Use --force only when intentionally replacing an existing generated HTML. The default protects existing output. Bundle version 1.0.0 accepts schemaVersion 1. Keep the versioned URL pinned during a task. Download hashes and sizes are published at https://codesurf.io/releases/1.0.0/manifest.json.

## Investigate and author the tour

- Start with the user's exact question and relevant repository, pull request, or revision. Read actual source and enough surrounding code to verify the execution path.
- Find the real entry point and verify how execution reaches it. Cover the smallest coherent slice that answers the question, including relevant returns, errors, and recovery. State any unverified handoffs.
- Assume the reader is new to the product and repository. Orient them in the opening step, explain each important function's purpose, inputs, and result, and use one concept per step.
- Include exact source text, preserving indentation, blank lines, comments, and whitespace. Use full repository-relative paths and original one-based line numbers. Include enough surrounding code for useful context. The renderer owns syntax highlighting and formatting.
- Include only the source needed for the tour. Use files[].startLine when an excerpt begins after line 1. Keep missing regions in separate file entries with their correct offsets. Explain omitted source in the step text. Never concatenate noncontiguous snippets and assign misleading line numbers.
- Include files[].revision and an HTTPS files[].sourceUrl pinned to the relevant commit when available. Do not include credentials, secrets, or unrelated private data.
- Build cards around coherent functions or related blocks. Set card.relevant to the exact important ranges. The viewer mutes other lines and folds irrelevant runs longer than 10 lines. Add outlines to label folded methods.
- Write explanation as text segments. Attach target to a meaningful phrase whenever it refers to source. This creates the official sidebar link that highlights and navigates to the exact code lines. Every reference target is automatically expanded at its step.
- Define connections using exact source and destination lines, a brief label describing the verified relationship, and kind call, event, return, success, or failure.
- Introduce cards and connections through cumulative step revealCards and revealConnections. A connection may be introduced only when both cards are visible. Each step must focus a visible code range. Back restores the earlier reveal state.
- For PRs and bug fixes, use separate before and after file entries with exact source and revisions, even when they have the same path. Mark cards with diff before or after and supply changedLines. Explain the old behavior and exact changed lines responsible for the fix. Distinguish source behavior from production outcomes.
- Use automatic layout first. Optional card x and y placement hints can refine a complex graph. The viewer recalculates arrow endpoints after layout or folds change.

## Preserve the official UI

Do not ask the LLM to recreate or restyle the viewer. Generate the JSON and package it with the official download. The versioned viewer supplies the light background, tour sidebar, code cards, line gutters, selectable syntax-highlighted source, folds, labeled arrows, source-row colors, Back/Next/Exit/Restart, pan, zoom, and Fit.

Study the official demo and reference screenshots to understand the expected presentation. Match their information density and teaching structure when choosing card ranges and tour steps. Code formatting and sidebar references are critical. Preserve exact source and use structured target links rather than handwritten HTML.

Official viewer screenshots:
- Opening step and folded context: https://codesurf.io/examples/viewer-v1/beginning.jpg
- Expanded source formatting: https://codesurf.io/examples/viewer-v1/code-formatting.jpg
- Sidebar phrase linked to highlighted source: https://codesurf.io/examples/viewer-v1/sidebar-reference.jpg
- Intermediate reveal and arrows: https://codesurf.io/examples/viewer-v1/middle.jpg
- Failure path and keyboard-focused reference: https://codesurf.io/examples/viewer-v1/failure-path.jpg
- Final step and complete graph: https://codesurf.io/examples/viewer-v1/end.jpg

Earlier design references (the official viewer defines the current UI):
- Beginning: https://codesurf.io/examples/walkthrough/beginning.jpg
- Middle: https://codesurf.io/examples/walkthrough/middle.jpg
- End: https://codesurf.io/examples/walkthrough/end.jpg

## Verify and deliver

- Run the validator and correct every schema, range, missing-ID, or hidden-reference error.
- Open the generated HTML. Advance from the first step to the last and back. Verify sidebar links highlight and navigate to the intended code, referenced lines are expanded, real line numbers stay correct, folds work, arrows meet their endpoint rows, and Exit tour reveals the full flow.
- Verify pan, zoom, Fit, and horizontal code scrolling. Keep code text selectable.
- Give the user the standalone HTML file. It includes its source snapshot and the viewer and works offline. Report any behavior you could not verify.
- In conversational follow-up, stay on the current step and advance only when the user asks.
- To revise the explanation, update the JSON and rerun the packager. Preserve the viewer.
